g_policy.reason: The offer is an opt-in button, the copy states the reward ($1 to PayPal), declining changes nothing, and the 'if the ad fails' field hides the button and sends no money when no game is ready.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is '1 US dollars paid to the player's PayPal', which is money, so it is cash.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is the player tapping Play with 0 lives, which is an app event, and no chat content is involved.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing free; lives, the timer, and the gold-bar button all work as today.

g_brand_safety.reason: The button sits in the s02 out-of-lives modal, which is rated safe and opened by an app event, over a non-chat screen (s01, safe).

c1_revealed_value.reason: As an existing_anchor, the reward must be a resource the app charges for or limits. The reward is a PayPal dollar, which the app neither sells nor limits (it limits lives, m01), so the check fails.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about 5 lives, the 30-minute regeneration, and gold bars bought with real money are supported by m01, m02, s02.e02, and s02.e03. The proposal adds the dollar reward and the new screen itself.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The product model shows no subscription (m02), so there are no paying plan members to spare.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is not a lasting grant of a charged item and takes nothing from other users, so it does not hit any c4 fail condition.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears in the out-of-lives modal right after the limit is hit, which is a moment of need.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The unit is a play-to-earn rewarded playable, the reward is paid only when the game counts as verified ('If the game doesn't count, no money is sent'), and the trigger is a detectable app event.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the out-of-lives pop-up (s02), the gold-bar button, the 5-life limit, and the 30-minute timer, which are specific to this app.

other_concern: The reward is $1 of real cash paid per game, up to 3 per day, which is a cost for the app and does not fit a lives-based monetization. The reward would be better as lives. The pitch also says it does not touch gold-bar sales, but paying cash competes with them.
